samples.summary: CSV formula neutralization also rewrites `sheets export --file-format csv`, corrupting exported formulas and any export→import round trip
samples.evidence: `neutralizeFormula` is applied unconditionally inside `formatCsv`'s `csvEscape` (csv.ts:42-52). `formatCsv` is not only used for `--format csv` display output: `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46` calls `formatCsv(res.data)` to write the exported spreadsheet file. Every exported cell `formula` (`=SUM(A1:A2)`) and every non-numeric value starting with `-`/`+`/`@` now gets a literal `'` prepended in the written file. Re-importing that file with `sheets import` (parseCsv → buildCellMap, sheets-import.ts:73-81) stores `'=SUM(A1:A2)` as a text value, so an export/import round trip silently mangles the sheet's data. No test covers the sheets-export path with the new neutralizer.

samples.summary: Callback server rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header, which risks refusing the genuine browser redirect on browsers/proxies that attach one
samples.evidence: `if (req.method !== 'GET' || req.headers.origin !== undefined) { 403 }`. The real callback arrives as a cross-origin 302 redirect from the backend; if any browser, extension, or corporate proxy attaches an `Origin` (e.g. `Origin: null` on cross-origin redirect chains), the legitimate code is refused and, because the 403 branch deliberately never settles the promise (line 227-233), `waitForCallback()` hangs until the 30s timeout and login fails with a timeout error the user cannot diagnose. Only node `fetch` (which never sets Origin unless asked) is exercised in packages/cli/test/login.test.ts.

samples.summary: A nonce that fails `parseCliNonce` (or an older backend) silently degrades to a 30s login hang instead of a diagnosable error
samples.evidence: `parseCliNonce(req.query?.nonce)` returns `undefined` for any nonce outside `/^[0-9a-f]{32,128}$/`; the state is then stored without a nonce and `auth.controller.ts:131-133` emits no `&state=`. The new CLI (`login.ts:227`) 403s that redirect and never settles the wait, so the user sees only 'Login timed out' after 30s. The same shape happens for a new CLI talking to a backend deployed before this change. Neither side reports the mismatch; failing fast (e.g. BadRequest when `mode=cli` and the nonce param is present but invalid) would surface it.

samples.summary: `cells batch --dry-run` bypasses the new `--format` validation and the surrounding try/catch
samples.evidence: The dry-run block was hoisted out of the try at cells.ts:147-155, and `parseOutputFormat` now runs only in the second try (line 158). So `sheets cells batch doc-1 --data '{}' --dry-run --format bogus` prints the dry-run body and exits 0, whereas docs/design/cli.md:1104 states an unsupported `--format` is INVALID_FORMAT/exit 1 for any command (and every other command validates before its dry-run branch, e.g. docs.ts:101). Additionally, `getConfig(opts)`/`printDryRun` now sit outside any try, so a throw there becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of the `{error:{...}}` envelope the rest of the handler guarantees.

samples.summary: New `cell()` JSON-serialization is only applied to the single-object path; array rows still render nested values as `[object Object]`
samples.evidence: `formatRecord` uses `cell(record[k])` (line 24), but the array branch still computes widths and cells with `String(row[key] ?? '')` (lines 46 and 53). Any list payload containing a nested object/array column (e.g. a document with nested metadata under `--format table`) still prints `[object Object]`, and the column width is computed from that same wrong string, so the fix is inconsistent with its own stated intent ('Mirrors what formatCsv already does').

samples.summary: Values containing `\r` are neutralized but never quoted, producing malformed CSV
samples.evidence: `FORMULA_TRIGGER` now explicitly covers `\r` (line 6) and the test asserts the output line is `'\r=cmd` unquoted. The quoting condition at line 48 only checks `,`, `"` and `\n`, so a value containing a carriage return is emitted raw; CSV parsers (and the CLI's own `parseCsv`) treat CR as a record terminator, splitting one row into two. Adding `\r` to the quoting condition fixes it.

finding.summary: CSV formula neutralization also rewrites `sheets export --file-format csv`, corrupting exported formulas and any export→import round trip
finding.evidence: `neutralizeFormula` is applied unconditionally inside `formatCsv`'s `csvEscape` (csv.ts:42-52). `formatCsv` is not only used for `--format csv` display output: `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46` calls `formatCsv(res.data)` to write the exported spreadsheet file. Every exported cell `formula` (`=SUM(A1:A2)`) and every non-numeric value starting with `-`/`+`/`@` now gets a literal `'` prepended in the written file. Re-importing that file with `sheets import` (parseCsv → buildCellMap, sheets-import.ts:73-81) stores `'=SUM(A1:A2)` as a text value, so an export/import round trip silently mangles the sheet's data. No test covers the sheets-export path with the new neutralizer.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `neutralizeFormula` (csv.ts:23-26) is applied unconditionally to every key and value in `formatCsv`'s `csvEscape` (csv.ts:42-52), with no opt-out. `sheets-export.ts:46` uses that same `formatCsv` to produce the bytes written to disk at `sheets-export.ts:51`, so this is a data-serialization path, not only a display path. The exported payload genuinely contains formulas — the backend returns `formula: cell?.f ?? null` per cell (cells.controller.ts:60-65) — so `=SUM(A1:A2)` is written as `'=SUM(A1:A2)`, and non-numeric values starting with `-`/`+`/`@` are also rewritten (PLAIN_NUMBER, csv.ts:12, exempts only numerics). On re-import, csv-parse.ts:82-97 `buildCellMap` stores the field verbatim as `{ value }`, carrying the injected `'` into cell data as text. No guard, caller check, or alternate writer makes the export path bypass the neutralizer, so `already-guarded` does not apply; silent alteration of persisted exported content is data mangling and squarely within the correctness lane, so `out-of-scope` does not apply. One supporting detail is overstated: the export shape (`ref,value,formula,style` header plus rows) is not cleanly re-importable via `buildCellMap` even without the neutralizer, since header cells land as data — but that weakens only the round-trip framing, not the core defect that exported cell content is silently rewritten. No test exercises the sheets-export path with the neutralizer (formatCsv is only covered in test/output.test.ts:82-152).

finding.summary: Callback server rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header, which risks refusing the genuine browser redirect on browsers/proxies that attach one
finding.evidence: `if (req.method !== 'GET' || req.headers.origin !== undefined) { 403 }`. The real callback arrives as a cross-origin 302 redirect from the backend; if any browser, extension, or corporate proxy attaches an `Origin` (e.g. `Origin: null` on cross-origin redirect chains), the legitimate code is refused and, because the 403 branch deliberately never settles the promise (line 227-233), `waitForCallback()` hangs until the 30s timeout and login fails with a timeout error the user cannot diagnose. Only node `fetch` (which never sets Origin unless asked) is exercised in packages/cli/test/login.test.ts.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as quoted: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:214 rejects with 403 when `req.headers.origin !== undefined`, before the nonce check, and the branch returns at line 218 without settling callbackPromise (resolve only happens at 274-277). The only escape is the 30s timeout at 280-288, so any legitimate callback carrying an Origin header results in a hang and an undiagnosable 'Login timed out' failure. The real callback is genuinely a cross-origin browser redirect: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:134-135 issues res.redirect to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback, so this request must pass the line 214 check. Tests only cover an explicitly attached Origin being refused (packages/cli/test/login.test.ts:81-99) and bare Node fetch for happy paths, so the failure mode is untested. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, no caller or upstream normalization strips the Origin header (sole call site login.ts:35/54), and an unsettled promise breaking the login flow is squarely in the correctness lane. Conforming browsers do not attach Origin to GET navigations, which makes the trigger unlikely, but that is external-spec reasoning I cannot ground in this repo and it does not cover header-injecting proxies or extensions; per the rubric, uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: `cells batch` parses `--data`/stdin JSON outside the try block, so malformed input becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of the structured error body the diff's own rationale relies on
finding.evidence: cells.ts:117-127: `cells = JSON.parse(dataStr)` (line 119) and the stdin `JSON.parse` (line 126) sit above the `try` that starts at line 139. In an async commander action a throw here rejects the returned promise; `bin.ts` (line 27, `program.parse()`) installs no rejection handler, so `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc --data '{'` prints a raw stack trace / triggers an unhandled-rejection crash rather than the `{ "error": { ... } }` body §8.1 promises. Pre-existing, but it is the exact failure mode the schema.ts hunk of this change cites ("bin.ts has no top-level handler") and adjacent to the modified try blocks.

verdict.reason: The finding describes code that is not in the repository. In packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts the `cells batch` action has exactly one JSON.parse (line 135) and it is INSIDE a try block opening at line 123; the stdin drain loop (lines 129-133) is inside the same try, and the catch at lines 136-145 calls outputError() with an "Invalid JSON cell data..." message and returns. There is no JSON.parse at lines 119 or 126 (lines 117-121 are a comment explaining exactly this guard), and the try at line 157 wraps the HTTP call, not the parse. The second claimed fact is also wrong: packages/cli/src/bin.ts is 6 lines with no `program.parse()` and no line 27; it calls runCli() (bin.ts:6), and runCli in packages/cli/src/cli.ts:71-92 awaits program.parseAsync() inside a try whose catch funnels every unhandled throw into outputError(e) (cli.ts:90). So both the alleged unguarded parse and the alleged absent top-level handler are contradicted by the working tree; malformed --data/stdin produces the structured error body, not an unhandled rejection.
